USER TURN 243
and file nameign descripmitnatl kunion good types?

ASSISTANT TURN 243 (1 messages, last privileged)
[earlier] Yes—those belong explicitly in the design too. ```text Naming Descriptive two-to-three-word names by responsibility: wakeup_commands.rs delivery_outcomes.rs schedule_repository.rs Avoid important modules named utils.rs, types.rs or manager.rs. Keep conventional Rust entrypoints such as lib.rs. Types Newtypes distinguish ScheduleId, WakeupId, RunId and DeliveryId. No interchangeable string IDs inside domain logic. Rust enums with associated data represent valid alternatives. Avoid bags of optional fields that permit impossible combinations. ``` For example: ```rust enum FirstFireOutcome { Fired { occurrence: WakeupOccurrence }, Cancelled { wakeup_id: WakeupId }, Paused { wakeup_id: WakeupId }, } ``` CLI maps cancelled/paused outcomes to explicit errors; SDK callers match typed variants. Your “no enums” rule applies to SQLite status constraints—not Rust enums. Rust owns exhaustive domain validation; SQLite stores extensible values without `CHECK(status IN (...))`. The design must also distinguish domain types, wire contracts and database rows, with explicit conversions where their responsibilities differ. No unnecessary duplicate type layers.

Disposition precedes remediation. Do not spend the remediation allowance on prose taste, already-satisfied obligations, or findings without semantic effect. Do not force a mental-model break through correction: stop at `discuss-pathfinding` or the exact owner selected by `spec-program-review`.

Do not dispatch a second design reviewer after remediation. Switching review mode, reviewer lane, target label, caller skill, or resuming after scratch loss does not reset the boundary. Another design review requires explicit user permission given after the first review/remediation result is visible.

Parent verification is not mislabeled independent review. When it resolves every original finding and no unrelated or uncertain meaning remains, return the design terminal or planning handoff; never return `review-permission-required` merely to restate that a hypothetical second review would need permission. Return the original review identity, accepted findings, correction anchors, verification evidence, unresolved boundary, and `review-permission-required` only when another review is explicitly requested or actually needed because meaning expanded or remains uncertain.
